name: Ron Johnson
summary: Johnson advocates market competition, lower regulation and taxes, reduced federal spending and greater state and local authority. He supports strong national defense and alliances while emphasizing limited resources and national interests; his later statements qualify his support for tariffs and favor state-level compromises on abortion.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: He opposed the proposed minimum-wage increase, arguing that it would destroy jobs and raise prices and that competition for workers should raise pay.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He argues that consumer choice and free-market competition deliver better health-care quality and prices than government control.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: He advocates competitive low tax rates and preserving the 2017 tax law rather than substantially increasing rates; this is a general tax stance rather than a proposed special rate for the wealthy.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He argues that unnecessary business regulations raise costs and obstruct innovation, and calls for removing them.

surveillance-ok.rationale: He voted for the 2011 Patriot Act extensions and the 2012 FISA reauthorization, against cloture on the 2014 USA Freedom Act, and defended the lone-wolf surveillance provision after the Orlando attack.

limit-guns.rationale: He joined the Supreme Court brief opposing New York’s restrictive licensing of civilian public carry and supporting the right to bear arms outside the home.

decide-locally.rationale: He says most governing should occur at state and local levels and education decisions should be made close to classrooms.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: He describes the constitutional marriage ruling as settled and offered to support federal recognition with stronger religious protections, but opposed advancing the 2022 bill without those protections.

abortion-legal.rationale: His later position favors a state referendum and describes a roughly twelve-week limit as a reasonable compromise, moving away from a conception-based ban but retaining substantial restrictions.

gender-social-construct.rationale: He cosponsored legislation defining eligibility in women’s sports through reproductive biology and genetics at birth, rather than gender identity.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He explicitly rejects ceding American sovereignty to international governing organizations and demands Senate scrutiny of major international agreements.

free-trade.rationale: He describes himself as supporting free and fair trade and stresses export opportunities, while allowing exceptions for security and unequal trade practices.

nation-first.rationale: He said a 2024 foreign aid package should not pass before the US secures its own border, and describes US sovereignty as something the WHO draft would erode.

open-borders.rationale: He demands secure borders and enforcement of immigration and removal laws, explicitly opposing policies he characterizes as incentives for unlawful entry.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He rejects the claim that large expenditures can significantly change the climate and favors adaptation over an accelerated fossil-fuel phaseout.

tax-inheritance.rationale: He cosponsored the Death Tax Repeal Act to end the federal estate tax, which the release calls a purely punitive tax.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: In his 2025 interview he supports reshoring essential products and fairer trade but warns that tariffs increase prices and damage exporters; he remains uncertain whether the benefits will outweigh the costs.

direct-votes.rationale: He advocates a one-time state referendum to settle abortion policy; the evidence supports this use of direct voting rather than replacement of representative lawmaking generally.

military-superiority.rationale: He calls for maintaining a decisive military deterrent while acknowledging finite resources and the need for spending scrutiny.

school-vouchers.rationale: He endorses school choice and publicly funded scholarship and voucher programs, including the District of Columbia and Milwaukee programs.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: He calls for reversing the pandemic-era spending increase and reducing deficits and debt, including large spending reductions; he does not give a comprehensive rule for every recession.

work-for-welfare.rationale: His agricultural policy record endorses reviewing SNAP waivers so that work requirements apply to able-bodied adults.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: He calls for allowing private producers to extract more fossil energy to lower energy prices, within a market-based energy strategy.

separated-powers.rationale: He insists that presidential international agreements remain subject to the Senate’s constitutional treaty-review authority.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Although preferring renewed negotiations, he supported imposing a railway labor agreement to prevent a strike and its economic consequences.

party-controls-media.rationale: On the floor he warned that giving the WHO a leading role against misinformation leads to censorship and suppression of free speech, and he demanded Twitter explain its removal of his post.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: His foreign-policy statement rejects transferring sovereignty to international governing bodies.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He calls for preserving and strengthening alliances as part of a realistic national-security strategy.

death-penalty.rationale: He cosponsored the Thin Blue Line Act, which adds killing a police officer as an aggravating factor in federal death-penalty cases.

religious-exemptions.rationale: He demanded stronger protections against government penalties for religious organizations whose marriage practices conflict with the federal recognition bill.

no-bailouts.rationale: He voted for the 2013 amendment ending too-big-to-fail subsidies for large banks and for 2011 amendments to stop taxpayers backing Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: He explicitly rejects reshoring all manufacturing, advocating diversified foreign supply chains while bringing strategically vital production home.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He joined a brief treating the Second Amendment as an enforceable constitutional protection against legislative restrictions on public carry.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: He cosponsored the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act, which defines sex in Title IX solely by reproductive biology and genetics at birth.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He identifies national defense as the federal government’s first responsibility and supports maintaining and funding the armed forces.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He supports stronger existing alliances and a decisive deterrent against adversaries rather than withdrawal into neutrality.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: His cosponsored sports bill treats sex as biologically determined at birth; the evidence concerns that statutory definition.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: His participation in the public-carry brief supports a civilian right to bear firearms beyond the state’s security forces.

collective-bargaining.rationale: On the 2022 rail dispute he said Congress should not impose agreements between private companies and their workforce, and backed the agreement the railroads and unions had negotiated.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: He voted for the Republican balanced budget amendment in December 2011 and proposes statutory budget caps tied to population growth and inflation.

student-debt-relief.rationale: He calls the Biden cancellation proposal an unconstitutional transfer that is unfair to taxpayers and people who already repaid their loans.

farm-price-support.rationale: He supported expanded federal food purchases and reopening dairy margin coverage during the 2020 agricultural disruption, providing a limited record of protecting farmers against market shocks.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: He cosponsored the Employee Rights Act, including protections for workers against compulsory union membership or payments.

voter-id.rationale: He advocates documentary proof of citizenship for registration and photographic identification when voting through the SAVE America proposal.

close-ties-china.rationale: He identifies China as the largest foreign threat and calls for a stronger American strategic position against it.

notes:
Living person: no inferred answers. Reviewed the complete statement list across all themes, including earlier career material and later qualifications. Advocacy against vaccine mandates does not establish a general philosophy of self-ownership, and border enforcement does not establish opposition to all immigration. The marriage answer records mixed evidence rather than treating opposition to one bill as an unconditional demand to prohibit same-sex marriage. Unknown answers are not positions attributed from party affiliation. Border restrictions are recorded separately from immigration levels: support for guest-worker and legalization proposals does not establish a preferred total immigration level. Source-access note: several Senate press releases timed out in the page viewer; their indexed full-text excerpts were read, alongside downloaded issue pages and interview transcripts. No unavailable text has been reconstructed.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 9 answers taken from it, 15 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Independent second pass (claude-sonnet-5-5), merged later with the first audit. Searched: about 550 senate.gov press releases and newsletters from May 2022 to Oct 2026 (full text via the site's RSS feed), all 5,017 Senate roll calls on Voteview, NPR/CNN transcripts in MediaSum. Themes searched with little or no stated position: universal health care, welfare and work requirements, Social Security reform beyond 'taxing the wealthy won't fix it', unions and strikes (only the 2022 rail dispute), immigration levels, Ukraine and NATO (his statements on Ukraine aid concern funding and a negotiated end, not the statements asked), federalism, term limits, filibuster (he urges ending it, but no statement asks about it), political violence, tech, space and nuclear power. Where words and record differ (trade) the answer is 0 at low. The Jan 6 2021 objection votes (no) and impeachment votes (not guilty) match no statement. Several senate.gov issue pages and Britannica/bioguide returned bot walls and were not used.
